correctness.rationale: The Sonine radial Fourier identity gives a Bessel J_{d/2+beta} tail whose L1 radial exponent is r^{-1-(beta-beta_c)}. Fixed-order large-r Bessel asymptotics uniform in a compact beta-neighborhood, periodic |cos| average 2/pi with bounded primitive, and an integrable r^{-2-epsilon} remainder yield the exact residue and uniform logarithmic window; local r=0 power is integrable. Independently checked the prefactor and numerical cutoff slopes at beta_c: d=2 0.6387808 versus A2=0.6366198; d=3 0.8082687 versus A3=0.8105695; d=4 0.9582345 versus A4=0.9549297. For finite TV, Cauchy–Schwarz applied to a signed spectral measure gives E|w|^2>=||mu||_TV^2 and sampling proportional to |rho| attains equality. At infinite TV, uniqueness of Fourier transforms of finite measures precludes any finite-variance unbiased all-displacement single-frequency representation. Scope expressly excludes other estimator families.
